summary: Throw any JavaScript value without coercing it to a CLR Exception object.

target.notes: Reuse the existing JsException wrapping representation used by ASYNC rules; a catch lowering must recover the original JS value.

semantics.evaluation: evaluate expression once, then create a throw completion carrying the exact value
semantics.identity: object thrown values are preserved by identity

caveats: C# forbids throwing arbitrary primitives or null directly.
Do not use this rule for throws inside async functions; ASYNC owns promise rejection conversion.

tests.name: primitive thrown value
tests.input: try { throw 17; } catch (e) { console.log(e, typeof e); }

tests.name: object identity preserved
tests.input: const x={a:1}; try { throw x; } catch(e) { console.log(e===x); }
